question: Why are newborns more at risk of drug toxicity from certain medications?

options.A: Reduced plasma protein binding leaves more free active drug
options.B: They consume a high-fat diet through breast milk
options.C: Their kidneys filter medications out of the blood too quickly
options.D: Their liver enzymes work twice as fast as adult enzymes

explanation: Newborns have fewer proteins in their blood to hold onto drugs safely, meaning more active medicine floats around freely. Makes sense when you picture it!

question: Why is a drug antagonist often compared to a broken key in a lock?

options.A: It fits the space but does not open the door
options.B: It falls out of the keyhole immediately after insertion
options.C: It destroys the lock mechanism permanently
options.D: It opens the door faster than the original key

explanation: Just like a snapped key fills up the keyhole so no other key can fit, an antagonist sits in the cell receptor without activating it. Simple and easy to picture!

question: Why would an occupational health nurse test the hearing of workers in a noisy textile mill?

options.A: To identify early signs of noise-induced hearing loss before it worsens
options.B: To check if employees are listening to unauthorized radio stations
options.C: To measure how fast the machinery is producing textile materials
options.D: To test the general intelligence and problem-solving skills of the staff

explanation: Loud factory noise can slowly damage hearing over time. Regular hearing tests (audiometry) help us catch any small changes early so we can protect the workers' ears.

question: What is the primary risk of pouring liquid disinfectant directly onto a digital weighing scale?

options.A: Liquid can seep inside and damage internal electronic circuits
options.B: It permanently locks the zero-adjustment mechanism
options.C: It causes the exterior paint to change color immediately
options.D: It will make the metal platform slippery for the next patient

explanation: Moisture inside electronic devices causes short circuits and rust, so nurses should use damp disinfectant wipes rather than pouring liquid. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why does stopping breastfeeding early increase a baby's chance of getting diarrhoea?

options.A: It stops the liver from storing adequate iron reserves
options.B: It forces the infant to produce too much stomach acid
options.C: It causes immediate permanent damage to the pancreas
options.D: It removes protective maternal antibodies that guard the infant gut

explanation: Breast milk is liquid gold for babies! It carries special antibodies that shield their delicate digestive system from germs while their own immune system is still growing.

question: Why is it so important to report an accidental needle-stick or blood exposure immediately?

options.A: Post-exposure preventative treatments work best when started quickly
options.B: Agency managers need time to discipline the careless worker
options.C: Insurance companies will refuse claims filed after twenty-four hours
options.D: State laws make late reporting a criminal offense for nurses

explanation: Time matters! Preventive medicines for bloodborne infections like HIV or Hepatitis B work best when taken very soon after an exposure.

question: What is the normal pH range for human blood?
explanation: Human blood must stay within a very narrow alkaline range of 7.35 to 7.45 for normal body enzymes to function. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T12#GNS121_U2_T12_h1)

question: What type of water is best for soaking Plaster of Paris bandages?

options.A: Ice cold water
options.B: Boiling hot water
options.C: Carbonated water
options.D: Lukewarm water

explanation: Lukewarm water gives you a predictable setting time. Hot water makes it set way too fast, and cold water slows it right down.

question: What is a great way institutional kitchens keep food costs under control?

options.A: Serving only imported luxury foods every single day
options.B: Eliminating all vegetables from the daily meal plan
options.C: Ignoring food waste and throwing away leftover ingredients
options.D: Practicing careful portion control and buying in bulk

explanation: Buying in large quantities and serving the right portions helps save money and cuts down waste.

question: What is the main difference between recording and reporting in the clinic?

options.A: Recording is writing down individual patient care, while reporting is summarizing data for higher health authorities.
options.B: Recording is done by doctors only while reporting is for nurses.
options.C: Recording uses electronic tablets while reporting uses paper only.
options.D: Recording happens once a year and reporting happens daily.

explanation: Think of recording as capturing what you do with one patient in front of you, while reporting is putting all those numbers together to send upstream so the government can plan public health! You've got this.

question: How does training hospital staff on equity and human rights improve everyday patient care?

options.A: It replaces the need for basic clinical nursing skills and drug administration
options.B: It legally forces nurses to work longer hours without extra financial compensation
options.C: It eliminates all infectious diseases within the hospital wards
options.D: It reduces unconscious bias and helps staff treat marginalized patients with greater respect

explanation: You nailed it! Equity training helps us check our biases so every single patient feels respected and welcome on the ward.

question: What is the first thing you should do when building a histogram from raw numbers?

options.A: Calculate the exact average of the categorical groups
options.B: Find the range by identifying the lowest and highest values
options.C: Color the bars using alternating bright shades
options.D: Draw the vertical and horizontal axes freehand

explanation: You always want to know your lowest and highest numbers first so you know how wide your chart needs to stretch!

question: When a nurse steps up to protect a patient's rights and safety, what role are they playing?

options.A: Advocate
options.B: Surgical operator
options.C: Pharmacist
options.D: Hospital accountant

explanation: You got it! Being an advocate means standing up for your patients' rights, safety, and best interests when they are most vulnerable. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to use data showing high rates of childhood malnutrition in a health plan?

options.A: Ignoring the data and focusing only on building a new staff office
options.B: Starting regular growth monitoring sessions at the primary health center
options.C: Setting up nutrition education classes using affordable local foods
options.D: Collaborating with agricultural extension workers to promote backyard gardens

explanation: A health plan must directly respond to identified problems like malnutrition, rather than spending resources on unrelated administrative projects. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h7)

question: A nurse wants to check old hospital files of patients who took a specific blood pressure drug five years ago to see who developed kidney issues. What kind of study is this?

options.A: Experimental trial
options.B: Retrospective cohort study
options.C: Cross-sectional survey
options.D: Case-control study

explanation: Well done! This design starts with a past exposure (the drug taken years ago) and tracks forward through old records to see what health outcomes happened.

question: What happens inside the body to cause muscle wasting (atrophy) during long periods of bed rest?

options.A: Rapid increase in slow-twitch muscle fibers
options.B: Excessive production of new muscle fibers
options.C: Protein breakdown happens faster than protein building
options.D: Permanent hardening of the bone marrow

explanation: Atrophy simply means muscles get smaller from lack of use. It happens when the body breaks down muscle proteins faster than it can build them up.

question: Why does not drinking enough water put pregnant women at higher risk for urinary tract infections (UTIs)?

options.A: Faster bacterial growth caused by extra dietary fat
options.B: Reduced flushing of bacteria from the urinary tract
options.C: Increased production of sugary urine by the kidneys
options.D: Lower body temperature slowing down immune cells

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Drinking plenty of water means regular peeing, which naturally washes away nasty bacteria before they cause trouble.

question: Which tool do nurses commonly use to check a patient's ability to handle daily activities?

options.A: Braden Pressure Scale
options.B: Katz Index of Independence
options.C: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.D: Apgar Scoring System

explanation: You got it! The Katz Index is the go-to tool for checking how well a person manages everyday tasks on their own.

question: Which type of diaphragm bends easily in half along a central hinge to make putting it in easier?

options.A: Flat spring
options.B: Coil spring
options.C: Rigid ring
options.D: Arcing spring

explanation: An arcing spring diaphragm folds right in half like a taco, which helps guide it smoothly into place over the cervix.

question: What special proteins does the body make to neutralize foreign invaders or antigens?

options.A: Enzymes
options.B: Antibodies
options.C: Platelets
options.D: Hormones

explanation: Spot on! Antibodies are the body's custom-built defense proteins that lock onto and disarm specific foreign invaders.

question: Which part of the small intestine connects directly to the stomach?

options.A: Jejunum
options.B: Cecum
options.C: Duodenum
options.D: Ileum

explanation: The duodenum is that C-shaped first stop where food leaves the stomach and meets up with juices from the liver and pancreas.

question: Why does quickly sorting (triage) a coughing patient help stop airborne infections in a crowded clinic?

options.A: It isolates infectious individuals away from the general waiting crowd
options.B: It eliminates the need for any staff personal protective equipment
options.C: It immediately cures the underlying respiratory infection
options.D: It guarantees that laboratory test results return within minutes

explanation: Brilliant nursing logic! Spotting coughing patients early and moving them away from other waiting patients stops germs from spreading in the waiting room.

question: What do we call the strong urge a teenager feels to fit in with their friends and social group?

options.A: Chronic poverty
options.B: Genetic predisposition
options.C: Metabolic tolerance
options.D: Peer pressure

explanation: Well done! Wanting to belong and fit in with a peer group is a powerful social factor that can sometimes lead teens to try things they normally wouldn't.

question: What does 'recall bias' mean in a retrospective study?

options.A: The loss of physical paper charts in a fire
options.B: Difficulty or inaccuracy in remembering past events
options.C: A computer error when deleting electronic patient files
options.D: The refusal of a hospital to share old records

explanation: Correct! Recall bias happens when patients struggle to accurately remember or report details about things that happened to them a long time ago.

question: Which cells in our nervous tissue are the main ones responsible for passing along electrical signals?

options.A: Fibroblasts
options.B: Neuroglia
options.C: Osteocytes
options.D: Neurons

explanation: Neurons are the star players! They are specially built to generate and send electrical impulses all over your body.

question: How is the daily amount of protein on a restricted diet typically calculated?

options.A: Percentage of total daily fluid intake
options.B: Cups per gallon of water consumed
options.C: Ounces per meal regardless of size
options.D: Grams per kilogram of body weight

explanation: Dietary protein prescriptions are personalized to the patient's body mass to ensure they receive enough for basic needs without overloading their organs. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h3)

question: How should a nurse present different contraceptive choices to a client?

options.A: By strongly recommending the most expensive brand in the clinic
options.B: Objectively, sharing both benefits and drawbacks of each method
options.C: By focusing only on permanent surgical options for parity
options.D: By hiding common side effects so the client does not get scared

explanation: Balanced presentation ensures the client makes a truly informed decision based on complete facts. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h6)

question: Which body regulates the professional scope of practice for midwives in Nigeria?

options.A: West African Health Organization
options.B: Nigerian Medical Association
options.C: Federal Ministry of Women Affairs
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria is the statutory body responsible for setting standards and regulating midwifery practice. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h2)

question: What was the main discovery of the Hawthorne Studies regarding workers?

options.A: Financial pay is the only thing workers truly care about
options.B: Strict physical rules eliminate all workplace errors
options.C: Attention and social factors heavily influence productivity
options.D: Workers perform best when left completely isolated

explanation: The Hawthorne Studies proved that human social interactions and attention from management boost morale and output. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which factor contributes heavily to nursing staff shortages in many Nigerian health units?

options.A: Mandatory retirement at age twenty-five
options.B: The migration of experienced nurses abroad
options.C: Strict laws banning hospital employment
options.D: A complete lack of nursing training schools

explanation: You're spot on. The 'japa' wave has caused many skilled nurses to move abroad for better opportunities, leaving local units short-staffed.

question: Who is primarily responsible for creating strategic plans in a healthcare organization?

options.A: Patient care assistants
options.B: Top-tier nursing executives
options.C: Shift charge nurses
options.D: Bedside staff nurses

explanation: Strategic plans are high-level organization-wide goals created by top leaders like the Director of Nursing or Chief Nursing Officer. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which physical item should the nurse inspect to evaluate medication adherence at home?

options.A: The electrical sockets for signs of dangerous overloading
options.B: The pill bottles or containers to check remaining doses
options.C: The family photo albums on the living room shelves
options.D: The kitchen trash can for discarded food wrappers

explanation: Inspecting medication packaging helps verify whether the client is actually taking their prescribed drugs on schedule. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is the simple difference between responsibility and accountability?

options.A: Responsibility requires no supervision, while accountability requires reporting
options.B: Responsibility applies only to doctors, while accountability applies to nurses
options.C: Responsibility is doing the task, while accountability is answering for the outcome
options.D: Responsibility is a legal term, while accountability is purely moral

explanation: You can be given the job to do (responsibility), but accountability means you answer for how it all turns out. You've got this!

question: What do biological indicators test for when placed inside a sterilizer?

options.A: The total weight of the metal trays loaded into the chamber
options.B: The correct color change of paper tape on instrument packs
options.C: The actual destruction of highly resistant bacterial spores
options.D: The exact temperature of the room surrounding the machine

explanation: Spot on! Biological indicators use real, super-tough live spores to prove that the machine is strong enough to kill the hardest-to-beat germs.

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand how the food supply works?

options.A: Community nutrition depends heavily on food availability and distribution.
options.B: Nurses are directly responsible for inspecting local food processing plants.
options.C: Hospitals must grow their own food to reduce patient feeding costs.
options.D: Clinical nursing duties include setting international agricultural trade policies.

explanation: As a nurse, you care for the whole community. If food isn't available or affordable, patients suffer from malnutrition. Understanding the food chain helps you connect the dots!

question: Which bone forms the large, flared upper part of the hip bone?

options.A: Ilium
options.B: Coccyx
options.C: Pubis
options.D: Ischium

explanation: The ilium is the broad, upper fan-shaped section of the hip bone that you feel on your waist. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T10#GNS121_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why do nurses collect clinical specimens like urine or wound swabs from sick patients?

options.A: To lower the patient's body temperature during a high fever
options.B: To test the cleaning strength of hospital floor soap
options.C: To replace lost fluids in the patient's bloodstream
options.D: To allow the laboratory to isolate and identify the exact pathogen causing illness

explanation: You nailed it! Lab specimens help find the exact germ making the patient sick so doctors can choose the right medicine.

question: What is a major cause of high antibiotic resistance rates in our communities?

options.A: Drinking too much clean municipal water
options.B: Eating fresh fruits and locally grown vegetables
options.C: Buying drugs over-the-counter and not finishing the full dose
options.D: Performing routine urinalysis testing too frequently

explanation: Self-medicating and stopping courses halfway trains bacteria to survive drugs, creating superbugs that are hard to treat.

question: Why is the VAPP Act's stance on marital rape considered a major legal milestone in Nigeria?

options.A: It recognizes that sexual assault can occur within a marriage.
options.B: It requires marriage counseling before any wedding takes place.
options.C: It gives husbands full legal ownership over their spouses.
options.D: It bans marriage for individuals under the age of forty.

explanation: Spot on! Older laws did not criminalize forced sexual acts between spouses, making this a massive step forward for human rights and safety.

question: Which of these is a clear example of vector-borne transmission?

options.A: A person drinking contaminated well water
options.B: Inhaling droplets from a patient's cough
options.C: Direct skin contact with scabies mites
options.D: A mosquito spreading the malaria parasite

explanation: You got it! Vectors are living carriers like mosquitoes that pick up a germ and deliver it to a human host.

question: What is the main focus of a National Drug Policy compared to a general health policy?

options.A: Pharmaceuticals and medicine supply chains
options.B: Medical doctor and nurse salary structures
options.C: Hospital building construction and maintenance
options.D: Global health donor funding negotiations

explanation: Think of it this way: while a general health policy looks at everything in healthcare, a National Drug Policy zooms in specifically on medicines—making sure they are produced, distributed, and used safely!

question: A patient taking daily prednisone reports sudden weight gain and swollen ankles. What is the best first nursing action?

options.A: Administer a stat dose of an oral antibiotic to prevent sepsis
options.B: Recommend doubling the daily sodium intake in the patient's diet
options.C: Instruct the patient to stop taking the prednisone immediately
options.D: Assess lung sounds and check blood pressure for fluid overload

explanation: Sudden weight gain and swollen ankles scream fluid retention! As a sharp nurse, your next step is to check how far that fluid has traveled by listening to lung sounds and checking blood pressure.

question: What is a 'Call to Action' (CTA) in an advocacy message?

options.A: A legal warning issued to government officials who delay funds
options.B: A list of symptoms used to diagnose infectious diseases
options.C: A medical emergency number to call during a disease outbreak
options.D: A clear instruction telling the audience exactly what to do next

explanation: You've got this! A CTA simply tells your listeners what practical step they can take right away to help.

question: Which surfaces in a patient's room need cleaning and disinfecting the most often?

options.A: The outer walls of the hospital storage cupboard
options.B: High ceilings and ceiling fan blades
options.C: High-touch surfaces like bed rails and door handles
options.D: The lower baseboards near the floor corners

explanation: You're right! Bed rails and door handles are touched constantly by hands, so they collect germs the fastest.

question: A nurse manager creates a ward schedule that requires double the current nursing staff, ignoring the hospital budget. Which principle of planning was violated?

options.A: Continuity
options.B: Flexibility
options.C: Feasibility
options.D: Secrecy

explanation: Feasibility means a plan must be realistic and work within actual available resources like budgets and staff numbers. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why does passing urine normally help protect your body from infections?

options.A: It physically flushes out bacteria before they can stick to the tract
options.B: It coats the bladder wall with a thick protective mucous layer
options.C: It neutralizes the pH of the urine to stop bacterial growth
options.D: It increases the core body temperature to kill pathogens

explanation: Think of regular urination like a natural tap flush! It sweeps invading germs out of the system before they can settle down and cause trouble.

question: What is a common physical sign of poor protein and nutrient utilisation in chronic illness?

options.A: Sudden increase in bone mineral density
options.B: Muscle wasting and delayed wound healing
options.C: Rapid growth of thick and shiny hair
options.D: Excessive physical endurance and high energy

explanation: You got it! When the body can't use nutrients properly, it starts breaking down its own muscle, leading to wasting and slow recovery from cuts or sores.

question: What is a simple, practical habit to ensure a patient gets a wide variety of helpful antioxidants and plant nutrients?

options.A: Eating a colorful variety of different fruits and vegetables every day
options.B: Eating the exact same single vegetable for every meal to track intake
options.C: Choosing only white and beige foods because they digest more easily
options.D: Relying entirely on multi-vitamin pills while avoiding fresh produce

explanation: Spot on! Different plant colors mean different health-boosting compounds, so eating a rainbow is always the best prescription.

question: A patient with severe diarrhoea complains of dizziness when standing up quickly. What does this finding suggest?

options.A: An acute blockage in the large intestine
options.B: Significant reduction in circulating blood volume
options.C: A sudden spike in systemic blood pressure
options.D: Normal recovery of gastrointestinal motility

explanation: Orthostatic dizziness indicates postural hypotension caused by volume depletion from excessive fluid loss through the gastrointestinal tract. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T7#GNS212_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is cooking with fresh, whole ingredients emphasized in a low-sodium meal plan?

options.A: It guarantees that the food will cook in half the usual time
options.B: It destroys all natural vitamins found in local tubers and vegetables
options.C: It allows the person preparing the food to control the exact amount of sodium added
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any water during the boiling process

explanation: Processed foods come pre-loaded with sodium, whereas raw, whole ingredients contain only natural, trace amounts of sodium. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h6)

question: What kind of infectious agent causes Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD)?

options.A: A slow-acting bacterial spore
options.B: An abnormally folded prion protein
options.C: A parasitic protozoan in brain tissue
options.D: A mutant strand of DNA virus

explanation: Spot on! CJD is caused by prions, which are unique proteins that misfold and don't even carry DNA or RNA. You've got this!

question: What is a major statistical risk when interpreting cross-sectional study results?

options.A: Using too many descriptive numbers in the final report
options.B: Failing to calculate the average age of the participants
options.C: Forgetting to write down the name of the hospital
options.D: Mistaking a simple association for a direct cause-and-effect relationship

explanation: Because you collect data all at once, you can't always tell which came first—the chicken or the egg (or in research, the exposure or the disease)!

question: When a patient experiences a permanent sensory loss, what emotional and psychological response do nurses frequently need to help them manage?

options.A: Grief, social withdrawal, and depression
options.B: Severe memory loss and confusion about time
options.C: Aggression and physical violence toward staff
options.D: Euphoria and unrealistic optimism about recovery

explanation: Losing sight or hearing is a massive life change. Patients often go through a grieving process and might pull away from others, so our empathetic nursing support is crucial here.

question: What kind of muscle makes up the external anal sphincter?

options.A: Smooth muscle
options.B: Cardiac muscle
options.C: Skeletal muscle
options.D: Elastic cartilage

explanation: Because the outer sphincter is made of skeletal muscle, you have voluntary control over it. It's what lets you hold it in until you reach a toilet!

question: How should a nurse respond when a patient insists their terminal test results belong to someone else?

options.A: Ignore the statement and change the hospital topic
options.B: Argue with the patient using hard medical facts
options.C: Agree with the patient that a mistake definitely occurred
options.D: Gently listen and avoid forcing immediate acceptance

explanation: Confronting denial too aggressively can cause extreme distress, so nurses should support the patient while remaining truthful. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why does a hurt or infected part of the body become warm and swollen?

options.A: Destruction of local nerve endings by invading bacteria
options.B: Decreased cellular activity slowing down the local metabolism
options.C: Rapid clotting of blood inside the deep muscle layers
options.D: Increased blood flow and fluid movement into the tissue

explanation: Correct! When your body sends extra blood and fluid to fight a germ at an injury site, it naturally causes warmth, redness, and swelling.

question: Why is a little bit of moulding considered a normal and helpful thing during birth?

options.A: It prevents the baby from breathing too early
options.B: It permanently seals the cranial sutures closed
options.C: It speeds up the dilation of the maternal cervix
options.D: It helps reduce the head dimensions to fit the pelvis

explanation: Spot on! By letting the bones telescope just a little bit, the baby's head safely adapts to the curves of the birth canal.

question: Which chemical group includes volatile liquids like acetone that can affect your nervous system when breathed in?

options.A: Corrosives
options.B: Solvents
options.C: Sensitizers
options.D: Carcinogens

explanation: Solvents evaporate easily into the air. When we breathe them in, they can travel through our system and sometimes affect our neurological function. Good to know for safe lab practices!

question: What is the main danger of giving a medication that another nurse prepared?

options.A: Patients prefer when the same nurse handles their entire admission
options.B: It violates hospital fashion rules regarding the treatment trolley
options.C: You cannot verify the accuracy of the calculation or sterility
options.D: The pharmacy department will run out of drug stock records

explanation: Always prepare your own meds when possible! That way, you are 100% sure of the math, the drug identity, and clean technique.

question: What is the main goal of surgical asepsis?

options.A: To kill all viruses while leaving bacteria alive
options.B: To reduce the total number of common bacteria
options.C: To eliminate every single microorganism and spore
options.D: To remove visible dirt and grease from the skin

explanation: You've got this! Surgical asepsis is all about absolute sterility—getting rid of every living germ and tough spore so nothing can cause infection.

question: When should used items in the home visiting kit be restocked?

options.A: Immediately after returning to the health clinic
options.B: Just before walking into the next patient's house
options.C: Only when a supervisor inspects the bag
options.D: Once every three to six months

explanation: Restocking right after returning ensures the nurse is always prepared for sudden emergency calls without delays. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h6)

question: Why is relying on a management theory better than being purely reactive in a hospital ward?

options.A: It guarantees that no nurse will ever feel stressed or overworked
options.B: It prevents doctors from making medication errors during rounds
options.C: It automatically increases the annual hospital financial budget
options.D: It gives leaders a consistent strategy to handle daily challenges

explanation: Structured theories help leaders plan and solve problems proactively instead of just firefighting daily crises. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why does getting pregnant at an older maternal age carry a higher risk of chromosomal issues in the baby?

options.A: The uterus loses its ability to protect the developing fetus over time
options.B: Sperm cells from older partners damage the egg's chromosomes
options.C: Primary oocytes stay arrested for decades, increasing the risk of errors during cell division
options.D: Hormone levels drop so low that follicles stop growing altogether

explanation: Remember that a woman's eggs stay paused in her ovaries for decades! Over time, the cellular machinery can get a bit tired, making errors slightly more likely during cell division.

question: Which safety measure is especially crucial in adult day care centers serving clients with cognitive impairment or dementia?

options.A: Restricted visiting hours for family members only
options.B: Locked individual client bedrooms for overnight sleeping
options.C: Mandatory physical restraints for all mobile participants
options.D: Secure entry and exit points to prevent wandering

explanation: Because many participants experience confusion or memory loss, controlled exits are vital to prevent elopement and ensure client safety. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h8)

question: What is the main goal of giving psychological first aid to an abuse survivor?

options.A: Prescribing antidepressant medications to cure trauma permanently
options.B: Offering immediate comfort, safety, and supportive listening
options.C: Forcing the survivor to report the incident to the police
options.D: Conducting deep psychoanalysis of childhood experiences

explanation: Spot on! Psychological first aid is all about offering a comforting presence, meeting basic needs, and easing shock without pushing unwanted counseling.

question: A patient refuses their home exercises and seems down. How should you view this as a nurse?

options.A: They clearly want their condition to deteriorate permanently
options.B: They are purposely wasting the healthcare team's valuable time
options.C: They have no right to question their prescribed care plan
options.D: They are likely overwhelmed and need support rather than judgment

explanation: When patients pull back, it's often burnout or emotional distress speaking. A little empathy goes a long way in helping them trust the process again.

question: What is the primary function of bile salts in digestion?

options.A: Digesting proteins
options.B: Emulsifying fats
options.C: Neutralizing stomach acid
options.D: Absorbing carbohydrates

explanation: Bile salts break large fat globules down into smaller droplets through emulsification, giving digestive enzymes more surface area to act upon. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal job of a healthy kidney?

options.A: Filtering and breaking down peptide hormones
options.B: Making large amounts of dietary insulin
options.C: Releasing erythropoietin when oxygen is low
options.D: Clearing parathyroid hormone from the blood

explanation: Spot on! Insulin is made by your pancreas, not your kidneys. The kidneys just help clear it out of your system later.

question: How does poor food purchasing directly affect patient outcomes?

options.A: It improves the patient's appetite significantly
options.B: It always results in immediate food poisoning
options.C: It decreases the overall cost of hospital stays
options.D: It can lead to nutrient deficiencies and health complications

explanation: Sourcing poor quality or inadequate food items deprives the body of essential nutrients needed for recovery and maintenance. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h1)

question: Which item is a major source of hidden sodium in many Nigerian home-cooked meals?

options.A: Fresh green vegetables
options.B: Seasoning stock cubes
options.C: Raw unrefined palm oil
options.D: Unprocessed yellow garri

explanation: Seasoning cubes are packed with sodium and are frequently added in multiple quantities to local soups and stews. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h5)

question: Why do nurses often recommend exit alarms or high door locks for homes with a dementia patient?

options.A: To prevent the patient from wandering outside and getting lost
options.B: To keep uninvited guests from entering the compound
options.C: To punish the patient for bad behavior during the day
options.D: To force the patient to stay inside their bedroom at night

explanation: Wandering can be very dangerous because patients easily get disoriented. Simple environmental barriers keep them safe inside.

question: What is the true relationship between FGM and major world religions?

options.A: Christian scriptures require the procedure for moral purity
options.B: FGM is a cultural practice falsely linked to religious texts
options.C: The Holy Quran explicitly commands all families to perform FGM
options.D: Islamic law strictly forbids any form of traditional surgery

explanation: Well done! Major religious books do not command FGM—the link is just a cultural misconception.

question: Which waste bin color is strictly designated for used sharps and needles in a Nigerian hospital ward?

options.A: Yellow bag
options.B: Green bucket
options.C: Black bin
options.D: Sharps box

explanation: Puncture-proof sharps boxes prevent needle stick injuries among healthcare workers and waste handlers. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the immediate first-aid action a nurse should take after sustaining a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Cover the tiny puncture wound tightly with adhesive tape
options.B: Wash the site immediately with soap and running water
options.C: Wait until the end of the shift to report it
options.D: Apply a tight tourniquet above the elbow joint

explanation: Immediate washing helps remove and flush out infectious pathogens before they can establish an infection. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h6)

question: What is the main job of the ductus arteriosus?

options.A: It carries waste products away from the liver
options.B: It pumps blood from the left ventricle to the brain
options.C: It connects the umbilical cord directly to the placenta
options.D: It directs blood from the pulmonary artery into the aorta

explanation: You're doing great! The ductus arteriosus acts as a bridge from the pulmonary artery straight to the aorta, helping blood bypass the resting lungs. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h2)

question: Why is watching a patient's brain function so important after heart tumour surgery?

options.A: The brain stops receiving oxygen if the patient lies flat
options.B: Tumour fragments or tiny clots could dislodge during surgery and cause a stroke
options.C: Patients with heart surgery always develop sudden memory loss
options.D: Anesthesia permanently damages the brain's visual cortex

explanation: Working inside the heart chambers can accidentally send tiny bits of debris or clots up to the brain. Neurological checks help nurses catch a stroke early!

question: A grateful family tries to give you an expensive cash gift for your home care. What is the right response?

options.A: Accept the gift privately to avoid hurting the family's feelings
options.B: Divide the money evenly among all members of the healthcare team
options.C: Keep the money as a bonus for providing excellent home care
options.D: Politely decline the gift while explaining professional boundary policies

explanation: It's a kind gesture from the family, but accepting expensive gifts compromises your professional objectivity. Always decline with kindness and grace.

question: Which of these is a major characteristic of adult learners during a teaching session?

options.A: They refuse to participate in group discussions or role play
options.B: They remember long lists of medical terms better than children
options.C: They need strict discipline and constant supervision from lecturers
options.D: They prefer to be actively involved in planning their learning goals

explanation: Brilliant! Adults love having a say in what and how they learn. They value their independence rather than just sitting quietly as passive listeners.

question: Which brain structure acts as the ultimate master control center for the autonomic nervous system?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Occipital lobe

explanation: The hypothalamus is the boss! It coordinates all visceral signals to keep your internal environment (homeostasis) stable and balanced.

question: What is the main purpose of nursing counseling during a woman's first pregnancy confirmation visit?

options.A: To build trust, provide essential health education, and address emotional reactions
options.B: To perform surgical procedures that permanently confirm the gestational age
options.C: To prescribe powerful medications that completely eliminate morning sickness
options.D: To diagnose underlying psychiatric disorders before the first trimester ends

explanation: Nursing is about care and connection! Early counseling helps moms process their feelings, learn good nutrition, and feel safe in your care.

question: What is the simple definition of poisoning in a clinical setting?

options.A: A chronic vitamin deficiency caused by poor dietary intake
options.B: Any substance that interferes with normal body functions after entering the body
options.C: An infection resulting from bacterial contamination in food
options.D: An allergic reaction to a newly prescribed antibiotic medication

explanation: You've got this! Think of poisoning simply as anything—a chemical, a drug, or a toxin—that disrupts how the body normally works once it gets inside. Great job!

question: What popular model explains that errors happen when multiple system defenses fail all at once?

options.A: The SBAR communication chain
options.B: The Swiss cheese model
options.C: The root cause hierarchy
options.D: The Just Culture pyramid

explanation: You got it! Think of safety layers like slices of Swiss cheese. Accidents only happen when the holes in every single slice line up at the same time.

question: A patient has a long-standing infection that cuts down blood supply, making the affected cells shrink. What is this adaptation called?

options.A: Hyperplasia
options.B: Atrophy
options.C: Hypertrophy
options.D: Metaplasia

explanation: Atrophy is when cells shrink and get smaller due to less work, poor blood supply, or chronic illness. Think of it as cells downsizing!

question: How does effective 'directing' help a clinical nursing team?

options.A: It builds trust, resolves conflicts, and prevents misunderstandings
options.B: It replaces hospital rules and regulations
options.C: It determines how many beds are needed in emergency
options.D: It automatically lowers medication costs

explanation: Good leadership and communication through directing keep the team happy, united, and working well together.

question: When would a nurse most likely need to insert a flatus tube?

options.A: Chronic diarrhea lasting longer than three days
options.B: Severe postoperative gaseous abdominal distention
options.C: A suspected complete mechanical bowel obstruction
options.D: Active and profuse upper gastrointestinal bleeding

explanation: Flatus tubes are super helpful when gas builds up painfully after surgery because the bowels are temporarily slow. Spot on!

question: What must a birth attendant do if a sterile item from the kit accidentally falls onto the floor?

options.A: Spray it with alcohol before using
options.B: Discard or replace the item immediately
options.C: Use it only if the floor looks dry
options.D: Wipe it clean with the kit soap and water

explanation: Once a sterile item touches the floor, its sterility is permanently compromised and it cannot be made safe for use again. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h5)

question: How do disease tracking and early reporting help control Lassa fever outbreaks?

options.A: They guarantee that no new rats will enter the village boundaries
options.B: They eliminate the need for expensive antiviral medications in clinics
options.C: They allow quick isolation and treatment of cases before the virus spreads further
options.D: They prevent the dry season weather from occurring each year

explanation: Catching and isolating cases early breaks the chain of transmission, keeping families and communities safe.

question: What is the best first step when walking into the hospital room of a patient with a visual impairment?

options.A: Stand quietly by the bed until they notice you.
options.B: Touch their shoulder gently to grab their attention.
options.C: State your name and role clearly before approaching.
options.D: Turn on all the room lights to maximum brightness.

explanation: Spot on! Always use your voice first so you don't startle them since they cannot see you enter the room.

question: When working in homes and local clinics, what is a community nurse's most powerful tool for delivering care?

options.A: Prescription drug formularies
options.B: The nurse's own self and relational ability
options.C: Hospital electronic health record systems
options.D: Advanced diagnostic laboratory equipment

explanation: You don't always have fancy hospital gadgets in the community! Your ability to connect, talk, and build trust with people is your greatest tool. You've got this!

question: When is active health surveillance most useful in a community?

options.A: Only when tracking patients who move to another country
options.B: When health workers want to reduce their daily working hours
options.C: When the health clinic has no paper, pens, or staff available
options.D: During a disease outbreak or targeted immunization campaign

explanation: Active surveillance means rolling up your sleeves and going out to hunt for cases. We do this when there is an outbreak (like cholera or measles) and every single hour counts!

question: Which of these actions is a serious breach of patient confidentiality?

options.A: Asking a mother for her child's immunization history
options.B: Discussing a patient's HIV status with neighbors at the market
options.C: Reporting anonymous malaria totals to the regional health office
options.D: Storing locked physical clinic registers in the facility record room

explanation: Never share private health details outside the clinic! Gossip destroys patient trust and violates professional ethics. What happens in the clinic stays in the clinic.

question: When would a patient with uterine cancer likely need radiation or chemotherapy after surgery?

options.A: As a replacement for surgery when the patient is very young
options.B: To restore normal menstrual function after the operation
options.C: If the tumor has high-risk features or has spread beyond the uterus
options.D: To prevent the initial development of benign uterine fibroids

explanation: Brilliant! Extra treatments like radiation or chemo are added if the cancer cells have started spreading further or look aggressive.

question: Which of these organs is found in the upper belly (abdominal) part of the abdominopelvic cavity?

options.A: Brain
options.B: Spinal cord
options.C: Urinary bladder
options.D: Stomach

explanation: Your stomach hangs out in the upper tummy area, while your bladder is tucked way down in the pelvis.

question: How is being 'hard of hearing' different from profound deafness?

options.A: Hard of hearing always requires immediate surgical intervention
options.B: Hard of hearing individuals retain some residual hearing capacity
options.C: Deafness is always caused by an infection in the outer ear
options.D: Deaf individuals can still understand whispered conversations easily

explanation: Patients who are hard of hearing still have some hearing left (residual hearing). This means devices like hearing aids can help them a lot!

question: Which workplace factor makes it hardest for employees to bring home-cooked food to their shift?

options.A: Lack of basic amenities like refrigerators and microwaves
options.B: The high cost of buying lunchboxes and food containers
options.C: Mandatory breaks that last less than two minutes
options.D: Company rules that forbid eating food brought from home

explanation: Without a safe place to store and heat food at work, employees have no choice but to buy outside meals or snack on dry foods. You're learning fast!

question: Which of these is NOT considered when deciding whether to stop a rescue attempt?

options.A: Duration of the cardiac arrest event
options.B: Initial heart rhythm and response to interventions
options.C: The patient's personal financial status
options.D: Presence of valid do-not-resuscitate documentation

explanation: Clinical care is based entirely on health factors and ethics, never on a patient's wealth or financial status. Good medical ethics at work!

question: What must happen first to let blood drain out of the penis when an erection ends?

options.A: Rapid contraction of the somatic pudendal muscles
options.B: Sympathetic vasoconstriction of the helical arteries
options.C: Complete structural failure of the tunica albuginea

question: Which two nutrients are most important for keeping older adults' bones strong?

options.A: Vitamin C and iron
options.B: Sodium and potassium
options.C: Calcium and vitamin D
options.D: Vitamin A and zinc

explanation: Calcium is the building block for bones, and vitamin D is the helper vitamin that lets the gut absorb that calcium!

question: Which type of sleep is mostly connected to dreaming and sorting out memories?

options.A: Rapid eye movement sleep
options.B: Stage one non-rapid eye movement sleep
options.C: Deep metabolic resting phase
options.D: Conscious alpha wave waking state

explanation: REM (Rapid Eye Movement) sleep is that active brain phase where vivid dreams happen and your mind processes everything you learned during the day.

question: Why can taking too many fat-soluble vitamins become dangerous?

options.A: All vitamins contain high levels of dangerous dietary sodium
options.B: Excess vitamins immediately turn into stored body fat
options.C: High vitamin levels completely stop normal digestion
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins can accumulate in the body and cause toxicity

explanation: Unlike water-soluble vitamins that wash right out, fat-soluble ones get stored in body tissues and can build up to harmful levels.

question: Why do nursing leaders study diffusion theories when introducing a new practice?

options.A: To predict the exact date the hospital will run out of medication
options.B: To understand why some staff accept new ideas quickly while others resist
options.C: To decide which patients are eligible for special treatments
options.D: To determine how much money a research study cost

explanation: You got it! People react to change differently. Diffusion theories help us understand human habits so we can bring our colleagues along smoothly.

question: What is the main goal of 'task-shifting' in mental health care?

options.A: Moving patients from local clinics to foreign hospitals
options.B: Shifting all healthcare responsibilities away from nurses entirely
options.C: Training non-specialized health workers to deliver basic mental health interventions
options.D: Eliminating the need for any specialized psychiatric services

explanation: Spot on! Task-shifting helps bridge the gap by empowering everyday health workers and nurses to offer basic mental health care where specialists are few.

question: What is a common ethical challenge for nurses working inside companies?

options.A: Determining how much profit the company should share with nurses
options.B: Deciding whether to charge patients high fees for emergency first aid
options.C: Balancing loyalty to the employer with the duty to advocate for worker health
options.D: Choosing which brand of hospital uniforms the factory staff should wear

explanation: It can be tough! Company-employed nurses sometimes feel pulled between management's business goals and their core duty to fight for the workers' health and safety.

question: What two main things interact during a serological test to confirm a microbe is present?

options.A: Peptidoglycan and crystal violet
options.B: Agar and nutrient broth
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide and catalase
options.D: Antigens and antibodies

explanation: You got it! Serology relies on the precise lock-and-key fit between the germ's antigens and our body's antibodies.

question: What is the main danger associated with shoulder dystocia during delivery?

options.A: Rapid tearing of the uterine wall at the fundus
options.B: Fetal oxygen deprivation due to trapped shoulders
options.C: Sudden severe infection in the maternal bladder
options.D: Immediate premature separation of the placenta

question: Which phase of disaster communication focuses primarily on hazard tracking and immediate safety actions?

options.A: Preparedness phase
options.B: Mitigation phase
options.C: Response phase
options.D: Recovery phase

explanation: The response phase happens during the actual emergency, requiring immediate real-time safety instructions. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h3)

question: Which scenario is a classic example of indirect contact transmission?

options.A: Getting infected with malaria from a mosquito bite during the rainy season

options.C: Developing a wound infection from direct contact with a draining sore
options.D: Inhaling large respiratory droplets expelled by someone coughing nearby

explanation: The shared pen acts as a fomite, transferring the virus indirectly from the coworker's hand to the new host's hand. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which sign is a classic clue that a teenager might be dealing with iron deficiency anemia?

options.A: Sudden and rapid weight gain
options.B: Hyperactive physical behavior
options.C: Yellowing of the skin and eyes
options.D: Chronic fatigue and tiredness

explanation: Correct! Low iron means less hemoglobin to carry oxygen around the body, leaving the teen feeling constantly wiped out and tired.

question: What actually happens during the 'promotion' stage of cancer development?

options.A: Mutated cells are stimulated to divide over and over
options.B: Cancer cells immediately travel to the brain
options.C: All abnormal cells safely destroy themselves
options.D: Normal DNA is completely repaired by enzymes

explanation: During promotion, things like lifestyle factors or irritants encourage those already-changed cells to keep multiplying into a bigger problem.

question: Which parasite is responsible for causing ascariasis?

options.A: Necator americanus
options.B: Ascaris lumbricoides
options.C: Enterobius vermicularis
options.D: Schistosoma haematobium

question: Why do younger adolescents frequently abuse household inhalants like glue and solvents?

options.A: They are prescribed routinely by pediatricians
options.B: They are cheap and legally sold household items
options.C: They do not cause any harm to the brain
options.D: They have pleasant long-lasting medical benefits

explanation: Inhalants are popular among younger teens because they are inexpensive, accessible, and easily found in everyday household products. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h2)

question: You are alone with a patient having a severe drug reaction. After stopping the IV, what should you do next?

options.A: Wait quietly for the next vital sign round
options.B: Run down the hall to find the head nurse
options.C: Call for emergency help while staying with the patient
options.D: Walk the patient to the treatment room

question: What should a nursing lecturer do first before using any instructional media in class?

options.A: Preview and test the material beforehand
options.B: Ask students to pay for the equipment
options.C: Hand out a surprise test on the topic
options.D: Turn off all lights in the classroom

explanation: Testing equipment and reviewing materials ahead of time prevents technical hitdrops and ensures smooth lesson delivery. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h5)

question: What is the main reason for writing a nursing diagnosis in a patient care plan?

options.A: To determine the total cost of hospital treatment
options.B: To replace the medical diagnosis given by the physician
options.C: To legally clear the nurse from liability
options.D: To guide the selection of appropriate nursing interventions

explanation: Correct! A nursing diagnosis highlights how the patient is responding to a health issue, which helps you decide what nursing actions to take next.

question: What is usually the very first sign a patient notices with oesophageal cancer?

options.A: Sudden vomiting of bright red blood
options.B: Progressive difficulty swallowing solids
options.C: Severe burning pain right after eating
options.D: Uncontrollable hiccups lasting days

question: What is a major long-term danger of untreated, persistent severe tachycardia?

options.A: Permanent freezing of the sinoatrial node pacemaker cells
options.B: Thickening of the heart valves due to high-speed blood flow
options.C: Heart muscle fatigue and possible heart failure due to constant strain
options.D: Complete blockage of all peripheral veins in the extremities

explanation: Just like running a car engine at top speed without a break, forcing the heart to race constantly wears it out over time, leading to muscle fatigue and heart failure.

question: Why does the nurse keep one hand hovering closely over an infant while they are on the scale pan?

options.A: To add extra downward pressure for accuracy
options.B: To keep the baby warm in a cold clinic room
options.C: To prevent the baby from falling off the scale
options.D: To stop the digital numbers from fluctuating

explanation: Infants make sudden movements and can easily roll off elevated scale pans, making close supervision a vital safety measure. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h4)

question: Where are primary immune cells like lymphocytes born and trained?

options.A: Kidneys and pancreas
options.B: Spleen and lymph nodes
options.C: Bone marrow and thymus
options.D: Liver and gallbladder

explanation: Think of the bone marrow and thymus as the ultimate training camp and academy where vital immune cells are produced and prepped for duty.

question: A nurse wants to document the exact number of malaria cases in a clinic last month. Which study type fits best?

options.A: Experimental laboratory design
options.B: Descriptive design
options.C: Explanatory design
options.D: Exploratory design

explanation: Correct! When you are just describing what is happening naturally without testing causes, it's a descriptive study.

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for patients managing celiac disease?

options.A: Mental stress directly converts into physical gluten proteins inside the gut.
options.B: Patients usually develop severe memory loss from carbohydrate withdrawal.
options.C: Strict dietary restriction and social isolation can create significant emotional distress.
options.D: Psychological counseling is the only proven cure for intestinal villous atrophy.

explanation: Living with a lifelong, rigid diet can feel isolating and stressful. Being a warm, supportive nurse makes all the difference for their mental well-being!

question: How can a severe lack of motivation among nursing staff endanger patient safety during a busy hospital shift?

options.A: Patients will refuse to take medications prescribed by unenthusiastic staff
options.B: Unmotivated nurses automatically lose their clinical license to administer drugs
options.C: Hospital administrators will immediately shut down the affected ward
options.D: Nurses may miss subtle signs of deterioration and rush through critical safety checks

explanation: When energy and motivation drop, it's easy to overlook small changes in a patient's condition or cut corners on vital safety checks. Stay sharp and stay safe!

question: A patient complains that the hallway is too bright and noisy to sleep at midnight. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Explain that hospital noise is normal and the patient will get used to it
options.B: Move the patient to a bed located directly at the nurse's station
options.C: Close the patient room door and dim the overhead lights
options.D: Call the doctor immediately to request a strong sleeping pill

explanation: Simple environmental tweaks like pulling the curtains, dimming lights, and shutting the door work wonders before reaching for medications.

question: A nurse notices a husband is dominating the conversation and suspects his wife is hiding health issues. What is the best first step?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately and document that care was refused
options.B: Scold the husband in front of the patient for interrupting the health history
options.C: Refuse to let the husband enter the clinic room during future appointments
options.D: Create a moment to speak with the patient privately without the husband present

explanation: Always find a safe moment—like stepping out for a lab test or a quick bathroom break—to talk with the patient alone so she feels safe to share what's really going on.

question: What is a key sign that a baby has pathological jaundice instead of normal physiological jaundice?

options.A: The baby feeding well and crying with a strong voice
options.B: Yellow skin fading completely by the end of the second week
options.C: Yellow color appearing within the first 24 hours of life
options.D: Jaundice showing up strictly on the third day after birth

explanation: Normal physiological jaundice takes a little time to show up. Any yellow color appearing on day one (within 24 hours) is a red flag that needs a closer look by the medical team.

question: What does 'full cost recovery' mean when pricing drugs in a DRF?

options.A: Recovering the purchase price plus all operational expenses needed to supply the drug
options.B: Selling the drugs at the exact same price the manufacturer printed on the box
options.C: Charging double the market price to make a large profit for the clinic
options.D: Waiting for the government to refund the pharmacy after all drugs are sold out

explanation: It simply means the price covers not just what the supplier charged, but also the extra costs of bringing the medicine safely to the pharmacy.

question: Why are hospice homes designed to feel homelike rather than clinical?

options.A: To reduce the anxiety associated with traditional hospitals
options.B: To encourage patients to continue active physical therapy
options.C: To make it easier for doctors to perform major surgeries
options.D: To lower operational costs for the healthcare facility

explanation: A familiar, comfortable environment helps ease the psychological stress and fear that patients often feel in sterile hospital wards. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h1)

question: What does client-centered care focus on the most when dealing with reproductive health?

options.A: The traditional beliefs of the senior medical doctors
options.B: The rigid scheduling needs of the hospital administration
options.C: The personal preferences and autonomy of the individual
options.D: The financial targets set by the facility management

explanation: Brilliant! Client-centered care puts the patient in the driver's seat, respecting their personal choices and rights over their own body. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h3)

question: What does a 'null hypothesis' usually say about two groups being compared?

options.A: The first group always has a higher score
options.B: The second group received a better treatment
options.C: There is no real difference between them
options.D: There are not enough patients in the study

explanation: The null hypothesis assumes a boring baseline: that your new treatment didn't actually do anything special and the groups are essentially the same.

question: Which finding in a patient's urine test often makes a doctor request an IVP?

options.A: Blood (hematuria)
options.B: White blood cells
options.C: Excess protein
options.D: Glucose

question: Why is psychological support also offered to the family members of a recovering patient?

options.A: To help them cope with stress and avoid caregiver burnout
options.B: To train them on how to perform physical therapy transfers
options.C: To evaluate their personal health insurance limits
options.D: To teach them how to administer prescription medications safely

explanation: Caring for a sick loved one is heavy work, both physically and emotionally. Supporting the family helps keep everyone healthy and strong!

question: Why is culturing and checking lab specimens so important for patient care?

options.A: It proves whether the nurse collected the sample at the correct time
options.B: It replaces the need for a physical examination by the attending doctor
options.C: It lowers the total cost of hospital admission for surgical patients
options.D: It helps medical teams choose the right antibiotic treatment quickly

explanation: You've got this! Growing and identifying the exact germ helps the medical team target the infection with the exact right medicine.

question: Which of these is a common physical sign of andropause?

options.A: Complete sterility
options.B: Severe ovarian atrophy
options.C: Increased visceral fat
options.D: Permanent voice deepening

explanation: As testosterone dips, men often notice changes in their body shape, such as building up a bit more belly fat and losing some muscle firmness.

question: Why do urinary buffers like phosphate and ammonia matter so much when the kidneys excrete acid?

options.A: They prevent water from being reabsorbed in the collecting duct
options.B: They actively transport glucose molecules back into the bloodstream
options.C: They supply the necessary sodium ions for the renin pathway
options.D: They bind free hydrogen ions so urine pH does not drop too low

question: How can a lower GNP indirectly lead to poorer health outcomes in a community?

options.A: By automatically increasing the number of trained nurses in rural posts
options.B: By eliminating the need for primary healthcare facilities
options.C: By limiting access to basic sanitation, clean water, and nutrition
options.D: By directly mutating viral strains in local communities

explanation: When money is tight nationally, basic needs like clean water and good food become harder for families to access, leading to more sickness. It's a tough reality, but understanding it helps us advocate for our patients!

question: What is the proper way to dispose of expired cytotoxic drugs?

options.A: Send them for specialized high-temperature incineration
options.B: Treat them in a low-heat autoclave
options.C: Pour them down the clinical sink with plenty of water
options.D: Bury them in a normal municipal landfill

explanation: Cytotoxic drugs have tough chemical structures, so they need intense, high-temperature incineration to be safely destroyed.

question: When must you clean your hands when wearing gloves?

options.A: Only when the gloves look dirty or torn
options.B: After removing them, but never before
options.C: Before putting them on and after taking them off
options.D: Only before putting on a fresh pair

question: Heparin is a common drug used to prevent blood clots. Where is it traditionally sourced from?

options.D: Porcine intestinal mucosa

question: How does a run chart help a nursing team look at their clinical data over time?

options.C: By predicting the exact date a patient will be discharged from the hospital
options.D: By distinguishing between normal everyday variation and unusual special cause events

question: Why should a nurse worry if a patient completely cuts out a major food group?

options.A: It usually lacks essential nutrients required for normal bodily functions.
options.B: It permanently damages the digestive tract within twenty-four hours.
options.C: It always costs significantly more money than cooking regular meals.

explanation: Our bodies need a mix of everything—carbs, proteins, fats. Dropping a whole food group usually leads to vitamin shortages. Well spotted!

question: What should you do with empty blood bags right after a transfusion finishes?

options.A: Throw them into the general municipal waste bin immediately
options.B: Wash them out with soap and return them to the patient bedside
options.C: Burn them in the hospital incinerator within five minutes
options.D: Retain them temporarily according to institutional policy

question: Why is keeping patient information strictly confidential so vital in HIV nursing care?

options.A: Confidentiality laws prevent laboratories from processing viral load tests

options.C: Hospital management disciplines nurses who share room numbers with doctors
