question: Which of the following is an example of participatory monitoring?

options.A: The health minister deciding project success without visiting the village
options.B: Community members tracking how many latrines they have built together
options.C: An external auditor writing a secret report in the capital city
options.D: A nurse counting clinic pills behind closed doors at night

explanation: Participatory monitoring involves the local people themselves measuring their own progress and output. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h8)

question: What common drink or food substance must a client avoid before having an EEG?

options.A: Caffeine
options.B: Red meat protein
options.C: Complex carbohydrates
options.D: High sodium foods

explanation: Caffeine is a little energy booster that stimulates the nervous system and can mess with normal brain waves during the test. Best to skip the coffee beforehand!

question: What type of observation happens when a researcher joins a group to experience their daily routine firsthand?

options.A: Non-participant observation
options.B: Participant observation
options.C: Structured observation
options.D: Laboratory observation

explanation: You got it! In 'participant observation', the researcher actively joins the community to get an inside perspective.

question: Which medication class is most commonly associated with causing orthostatic fainting?

options.A: Antacids
options.B: Antihypertensives
options.C: Antibiotics
options.D: Analgesics

explanation: Medications that lower blood pressure can sometimes drop it too far, especially when standing up, leading to fainting. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h3)

question: How do your regular monthly payments (premiums) help you during a major medical emergency?

options.A: It stops the disease from spreading to family members
options.B: It guarantees immediate discharge from the hospital
options.C: It draws from a shared pool to pay for expensive treatments
options.D: It doubles the amount of medicine the doctor can prescribe

explanation: Spot on! Contributions from many people create a shared financial pool used to pay for individual medical care when emergencies happen.

question: When does the incubation period of an infection officially come to an end?

options.A: The moment the pathogen is fully cleared
options.B: The day the person leaves the hospital
options.C: The appearance of the first clinical symptoms
options.D: The laboratory confirmation of antibodies

explanation: Spot on! The incubation period ends the very moment a patient starts showing signs or symptoms of being sick. You've got this!

question: What is the recommended minimum time gap between pregnancies to protect mum and baby?

options.A: Twelve weeks
options.B: At least twenty-four months
options.C: Six months
options.D: Five years

explanation: Wonderful! Waiting at least two years lets the mother recover her strength and nutrient stores, giving the next baby a healthier start.

question: In quantitative research, what is the main type of data you collect?

options.A: Numerical data
options.B: Descriptive text
options.C: Personal stories
options.D: Audio recordings

explanation: Think numbers and measurements! Quantitative research is all about gathering figures to spot patterns and trends. You've got this!

question: Why might a nurse position an abdominal ultrasound patient to lie on their left side?

options.A: To stop them from rolling off the bed
options.B: To shift bowel gas away from the organs being checked
options.C: To boost their blood pressure for the Doppler scan
options.D: To relax their tummy muscles completely

explanation: Shifting the patient's position helps move pesky gas-filled loops of the bowel out of the way of the ultrasound beam.

question: What do we call the mismatch when a baby's head is too big to fit through the mother's pelvis?

options.A: Uterine inertia
options.B: Secondary power failure
options.C: Occipitoposterior arrest
options.D: Cephalopelvic disproportion

explanation: Spot on! Cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD) simply means the baby's head size or the pelvis shape makes a normal vaginal delivery impossible.

question: About how much total cerebrospinal fluid does the human body produce every 24 hours?

options.A: 15 milliliters
options.B: 500 milliliters
options.C: 50 milliliters
options.D: 5 liters

explanation: You got it! Our bodies continuously refresh our CSF, making about 500 milliliters every single day.

question: During a home visit, which action shows you are doing a great psychosocial assessment?

options.A: Rushing through the checklist to finish documentation before leaving
options.B: Focusing solely on the physical wound care without talking to the client
options.C: Reviewing vital signs while ignoring changes in the client's personal appearance
options.D: Asking open-ended questions and observing environmental cues in the home

explanation: A great nurse looks beyond the medical chart. By asking open questions and noticing how the home looks and feels, you get the full picture of the client's world.

question: Which type of injury happens at the exact moment a physical blow or crash occurs?

options.A: Metabolic injury
options.B: Primary injury
options.C: Tertiary injury
options.D: Secondary injury

explanation: That's correct! The primary injury is the immediate damage that happens right at the time of impact, like torn tissue or bruising.

question: How do vitamins mostly help our bodies work?

options.A: Forming the primary structural skeleton of human bones
options.B: Serving as concentrated thermal insulation beneath the skin
options.C: Providing the bulk energy needed for intense physical exercise
options.D: Acting as coenzymes to help biochemical reactions run smoothly

explanation: Vitamins don't give you direct energy like carbs, but they act like little sparks or helpers (coenzymes) to keep your body's chemistry running smoothly.

question: Why is the sublingual route unsuitable for medications that require a large dose?

options.A: Large doses dissolve too quickly to be safe.
options.B: Large amounts will stain the teeth permanently.
options.C: Big pills cause the tongue to become paralyzed.
options.D: The physical space under the tongue is very small.

explanation: Only small, highly potent doses fit comfortably under the tongue for effective mucosal absorption. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h5)

question: You are assessing an elderly diabetic patient who lives alone. What is the best nursing action to help lower their risk of infection?

options.A: Evaluate blood glucose control, foot care practices, and home safety hazards
options.B: Recommend immediate admission to a long-term psychiatric care facility
options.C: Advise the patient to stop taking all prescribed medications immediately
options.D: Instruct the family to restrict all visitors from entering the home

explanation: Exactly right! Checking how well they manage their blood sugar and looking out for foot sores directly targets a diabetic patient's biggest infection risks.

question: If a hospital notices that drugs are sitting too long and expiring on the shelf, what should they do?

options.A: Stop all auditing procedures to save time and administrative money
options.B: Double the selling prices of all remaining stock to make up for losses
options.C: Force ward nurses to purchase the expired drugs for personal use
options.D: Review ordering patterns to buy smaller, more appropriate quantities

explanation: Expiring stock means they are ordering more than patients actually need. Adjusting the order size stops valuable medicine from going to waste!

question: A patient has an ideal body weight of 70 kg. Which tidal volume setting falls within the safe lung-protective range?

options.A: 750 mL
options.B: 450 mL
options.C: 900 mL
options.D: 250 mL

explanation: Protective ventilation uses 6 to 8 mL per kg. For a 70 kg patient, that's roughly 420 to 560 mL, making 450 mL a safe and correct choice!

question: Who chooses the Village Health Workers to serve in rural communities?

options.A: The federal minister of health
options.B: The community members themselves
options.C: International donor agencies
options.D: Private pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Wonderful! When the community picks their own health worker, it builds instant trust and ensures the care fits their local culture.

question: A patient with a medullary stroke has a weak gag reflex and trouble swallowing. What is the most important nursing priority?

options.A: Checking passive range of motion in the limbs
options.B: Applying warm compresses to the neck muscles
options.C: Preventing food or liquid from entering the airway
options.D: Encouraging high fluid intake by mouth immediately

explanation: Impaired swallowing and a weak gag reflex lead straight to aspiration and pneumonia, making airway safety the primary concern. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h6)

question: A nurse wants to improve child immunization rates in a rural town. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Handing out flyers written in a foreign language nobody speaks
options.B: Ordering all parents to bring children to the clinic without explanation
options.C: Partnering with local religious and community leaders to promote the clinic
options.D: Closing local markets until every child receives a vaccination

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with trusted local leaders builds instant trust and encourages parents to bring their children.

question: Why is it so helpful for nurses to involve family caregivers in the care plan for an autistic patient?

options.A: Caregivers know the patient's unique routines and communication cues best
options.B: Caregivers have formal medical degrees in nursing care
options.C: Hospital policy legally requires family members to do the nursing work
options.D: It removes all responsibility from the hospital staff

explanation: Family members are absolute experts on their loved one's specific triggers and favorite comforts. Partnering with them makes all the difference!

question: A fertility patient feels lonely and upset. What is the kindest and most professional nursing action?

options.A: Validate her feelings and offer information on support groups
options.B: Advise her to keep her struggles entirely private from family
options.C: Tell the patient to stop treatments immediately to save money
options.D: Explain that emotional stress has no impact on physical health

explanation: Listening, validating her feelings, and connecting her with others going through the same thing makes all the difference. You're learning to be a wonderful nurse!

question: How does regular physical exercise help lower a person's blood sugar?

options.A: By permanently curing pancreatic beta cell damage
options.B: By destroying excess sugar in the bloodstream
options.C: By increasing insulin sensitivity in muscle cells
options.D: By slowing down overall body metabolism

explanation: Exercise tunes up your muscle cells so they respond better to insulin, helping them pull glucose out of the blood much easier. Keep up the momentum!

question: What is the main difference between parenteral (injectable) and oral anticoagulants?

options.A: Parenteral agents are injected for fast action, while oral agents are swallowed for long-term use
options.B: Parenteral drugs only target platelets, while oral drugs target the whole clotting cascade
options.C: Oral medications are only used in emergency intensive care units
options.D: Oral agents never require lab tests, whereas parenteral drugs need daily blood checks

explanation: You got it! When we need a fast response in an emergency, we inject it (parenteral). For long-term home use, pills (oral) are much easier for patients.

question: What is the primary anatomical section of the small intestine responsible for the majority of active nutrient absorption?

options.A: Duodenum
options.B: Pylorus
options.C: Ileum
options.D: Jejunum

explanation: The jejunum has a thick mucosal wall with dense folds designed specifically for absorbing the bulk of digested nutrients into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T8#GNS213_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is the main reason we preserve food?

options.A: To completely eliminate all vitamins from food items
options.B: To replace natural food colors with artificial dyes
options.C: To stop or slow down food spoilage and microbial growth
options.D: To make food taste significantly sweeter and saltier

explanation: Food preservation stops germs and chemical reactions from spoiling our meals, helping keep food safe to eat later!

question: What makes a clinic truly "youth-friendly" when it comes to reproductive health?

options.A: Programs that focus solely on treating severe physical trauma injuries
options.B: Medical facilities that treat only patients under twelve years of age
options.C: Clinics that operate exclusively during late night hours on weekends
options.D: Services that offer confidential, non-judgmental care tailored to teenagers

explanation: Youth-friendly clinics win teens' trust by keeping their business private, listening without scolding, and treating them with absolute respect.

question: Which of these is a classic, telltale sign of digoxin toxicity?

options.A: Sudden uncontrollable muscle twitching in legs
options.B: Turning of the skin to a bright red color
options.C: Seeing yellow-green halos around lights
options.D: Complete loss of the sense of hearing

explanation: Classic nursing board exam favorite! Seeing yellow-green halos or fuzzy lights is a huge red flag that there is too much digoxin in the patient's system.

question: How does severe dehydration affect the skin?

options.A: It permanently changes the natural pigmentation of the skin
options.B: It speeds up the healing rate of minor skin abrasions
options.C: It causes an overproduction of natural skin oils
options.D: It reduces blood flow and impairs cellular metabolism

explanation: Well done! When your body lacks water, blood flow to the skin slows down, starving the cells and making the skin weak and fragile.

question: What is the main result you look for in a qualitative thematic analysis?

options.A: A laboratory value chart for patient diagnostics
options.B: A bar graph showing demographic frequency counts
options.C: Overarching themes that capture the meaning of the data
options.D: A precise statistical correlation coefficient

explanation: You're doing great! Thematic analysis groups all the interview notes into big, meaningful themes that tell the core story of the research.

question: What is a major danger of the social stigma surrounding abortion in healthcare?

options.A: Clients may delay seeking life-saving medical care out of fear
options.B: Hospital pharmacies automatically run out of emergency drugs
options.C: Infection rates drop because patients use home remedies first
options.D: Doctors are legally required to discharge patients within hours

explanation: Fear of harsh words or mistreatment often makes women wait too long to come to the hospital, which sadly makes their physical complications much worse.

question: How does poor transport infrastructure affect infectious disease surveillance?

options.A: It prevents nurses from washing their hands properly
options.B: It stops doctors from writing prescriptions on paper
options.C: It forces patients to walk to international hospitals
options.D: It delays getting biological samples safely to testing laboratories

explanation: Without good roads or transport, samples take too long to reach labs, slowing down outbreak detection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h7)

question: A community nurse notices a sudden spike in typhoid cases in a village. What is the best first move?

options.A: Close all schools in the country permanently
options.B: Order immediate quarantine for every healthy person in the region
options.C: Stop all routine vaccinations until the investigation ends
options.D: Investigate potential sources like local water supplies and food handlers

explanation: To stop an outbreak, you have to play detective! Tracking down contaminated water or food handlers helps you find the exact source.

question: Why is good lighting so important when checking a patient's skin?

options.A: To accurately observe subtle changes in color and moisture
options.B: To prevent the patient from feeling nervous during the exam
options.C: To warm up the skin surface before touching it
options.D: To make the physical examination finish much faster

explanation: Great lighting is your best friend! It helps you spot tiny color shifts and moisture levels so you never miss a detail.

question: What naturally happens to the outer layer of the skin as a person ages?

options.A: It becomes thinner and loses its elasticity
options.B: It produces significantly more sweat and oil
options.C: It permanently changes its original pigmentation
options.D: It grows thicker and develops more fat layers

explanation: As we age, our skin loses collagen and the epidermis gets thinner. This makes older adults' skin much more fragile and prone to tears or bruises. Good to keep in mind during daily care!

question: What is the main goal of medications called inotropes in acute heart failure?

options.A: To increase the strength of the heart's muscle contractions
options.B: To stop all electrical activity in the heart
options.C: To dissolve stubborn stomach ulcers
options.D: To lower body temperature during a fever

explanation: Inotropes act like a personal gym coach for the heart muscle, helping it squeeze harder so it can push more blood out to the body when it's struggling.

question: In many traditional Nigerian communities, how was maternal and child health viewed regarding fathers?

options.A: It was managed entirely by traditional birth attendants.
options.B: It was considered the primary duty of the local chief.
options.C: It was the direct responsibility of the federal health ministry.
options.D: It was viewed strictly as a female domain.

explanation: Historically, pregnancy and childcare spaces were culturally set aside for women only, which kept men out of the process. You're doing great!

question: What natural monthly bodily change affects an adolescent girl's need for extra iron?

options.A: Ovulation
options.B: Menarche
options.C: The growth spurt
options.D: Pubarche

explanation: Spot on! Menarche (the start of monthly periods) means the body needs to replenish its iron stores regularly. You're doing great!

question: What are the three categories assessed in the standard Glasgow Coma Scale?

options.A: Reflexes, muscle tone, and sensation
options.B: Pupil reaction, blood pressure, and heart rate
options.C: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response
options.D: Swallowing, speech, and balance

explanation: The GCS evaluates three distinct behavioral domains: how the eyes open, what the patient says, and how the body moves. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T6#GNS222_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is the immediate danger when a person's upper airway gets blocked?

options.A: High blood pressure all over the body
options.B: Too much lung fluid being made
options.C: Blocked airflow leading to low oxygen (hypoxia)
options.D: The tiny air sacs in the lower lungs get too big

explanation: When the upper airway is blocked, fresh air can't get through to the lungs. This causes oxygen levels in the blood to drop fast—a condition we call hypoxia.

question: Which model explains that people change their habits by moving through steps like thinking about it, and then finally taking action?

options.A: The Biomedical Treatment Model
options.B: The Environmental Sanitation Grid
options.C: The Germ Theory of Disease
options.D: The Transtheoretical Model

explanation: Well done! The Transtheoretical Model breaks down the journey of change from early thoughts all the way to long-term maintenance.

question: How does overall energy balance affect a patient's body weight over time?

options.A: Consuming more calories than expended results in weight gain
options.B: BMR increases infinitely whenever extra food is eaten
options.C: Weight changes only occur if fluid balance is disturbed
options.D: Exercise alone determines weight without regard to food intake

explanation: Energy balance dictates that excess consumed calories are stored by the body, leading to weight gain. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h5)

question: What is the primary point of entry for individuals into the national health system?

options.A: Private specialist clinic
options.B: Primary Health Care
options.C: National health ministry
options.D: Tertiary teaching hospital

explanation: Primary Health Care serves as the first level of contact for individuals and families entering the health system. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why is resource mobilization by the PTA necessary in many public schools?

options.A: Government funding is often insufficient to cover all needs
options.B: Teachers refuse to use their personal salaries for repairs
options.C: Parents prefer paying cash directly to health workers
options.D: Building infrastructure is strictly forbidden by law

explanation: Shortages in public educational funding make community contributions through the PTA essential for basic infrastructure. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h3)

question: How does proper birth spacing protect a mother's health?

options.A: It gives the mother's body time to recover nutrients and strength
options.B: It eliminates the need for any antenatal checkups
options.C: It completely prevents the onset of gestational diabetes
options.D: It guarantees that the next baby will be born full-term

explanation: Giving the body a break between pregnancies allows nutrient stores to refill, making future pregnancies much safer for mum. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h2)

question: A pregnant client at 32 weeks presents with sudden, painless vaginal bleeding, and an ultrasound shows her placenta is covering the cervix. What is this condition called?

options.A: Tubal ectopic pregnancy
options.B: Complete placental abruption
options.C: Spontaneous tubal abortion
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: You got it! Placenta previa happens when the placenta implants low in the uterus and ends up covering the cervix. Great job connecting theory to real-world nursing care!

question: Why are patients with significant hearing loss also at a higher risk for accidental falls?

options.A: Hearing aids pull the head to one side and throw off normal body alignment
options.B: Inner ear structures involved in hearing also help control balance and spatial orientation
options.C: Patients with poor hearing refuse to wear shoes with proper non-slip soles
options.D: The medication used to treat hearing loss causes sudden daytime sleepiness

explanation: Spot on! The inner ear doesn't just handle hearing—it also houses our balance system. When there's an ear issue, balance can take a hit too.

question: What role do descriptive studies play in nursing science?

options.A: They supply baseline facts that point toward areas needing clinical investigation
options.B: They replace clinical trials by proving which drugs cure diseases
options.C: They force patients to alter their daily health habits for better outcomes
options.D: They eliminate all errors found in previous medical journals

explanation: Descriptive studies act like our radar—they highlight where health issues lie, guiding nurses on what needs closer study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h2)

question: A patient in a disaster zone has a severe head injury, is unresponsive, breathing irregularly, and has no pulse. Which triage category fits best?

options.A: Red
options.B: Black
options.C: Yellow
options.D: Green

explanation: You're doing great. A black tag (or expectant) is used for catastrophic injuries where survival is sadly very unlikely, helping us save resources for those we can help.

question: Which sign warns you that the uterus might soon rupture during prolonged, difficult labor?

options.A: Formation of a Bandl's retraction ring on the abdomen
options.B: Clear and watery vaginal discharge
options.C: Decreased maternal heart rate
options.D: Low body temperature and shivering

explanation: You've got this! A visible retraction ring means the top part of the uterus is thickening while the bottom stretches dangerously thin. Such a crucial clinical catch!

question: What is the single most effective way to stop the spread of infections in the hospital?

options.A: Taking daily antibiotics
options.B: Wearing sterile gloves
options.C: Using room air filters
options.D: Proper hand hygiene

explanation: Simple yet powerful! Washing or sanitizing your hands properly is your number one shield against carrying germs from patient to patient.

question: How should you best care for a pregnant woman who has mild round ligament cramps?

options.A: Prescribing strong pain medications without consulting a doctor
options.B: Telling her to ignore all pain because it is completely imaginary
options.C: Admitting her immediately to the labor ward for IV fluids
options.D: Reassuring her about normal changes and suggesting gentle stretching

explanation: Warm reassurance and simple comfort measures are all that's needed for normal pregnancy aches. Keep up the brilliant work!

question: What is the main framework hospitals use to organize their response during an emergency?

options.A: Incident Command System
options.B: Routine Hospital Hierarchy
options.C: Private Insurance Network
options.D: Strict Quarantine Protocol

explanation: Great job! The Incident Command System (ICS) gives healthcare teams a clear, organized way to manage chaos during a crisis.

question: What is the key difference between quarantine and isolation?

options.A: Quarantine separates healthy people who were exposed, while isolation separates sick individuals.
options.B: Quarantine is managed in hospitals, while isolation happens exclusively at home.
options.C: Quarantine is used only for bacterial infections, while isolation is used for viruses.
options.D: Quarantine restricts animal movements, while isolation restricts human movements.

explanation: Exactly! Quarantine is for people who were exposed but aren't sick yet, while isolation is for people who are already confirmed sick.

question: Which type of vaccine uses a weakened live germ to give long-lasting immunity, often with just a few doses?

options.A: Inactivated
options.B: Subunit
options.C: Live-attenuated
options.D: Toxoid

explanation: Live-attenuated vaccines act like a mild natural infection, training your immune cells really well so they remember the germ for a long time.

question: What is the main job of hepatocytes inside the liver?

options.A: Producing red blood cells
options.B: Handling metabolism and clearing out toxins
options.C: Pumping oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation
options.D: Filtering waste through the kidneys

explanation: Hepatocytes are the hardworking main cells of the liver. They manage your metabolism, build proteins, and clear out body toxins every single day!

question: What is the job of pepsinogen once it is inside the stomach?

options.A: It converts into active pepsin to break down proteins
options.B: It lines the stomach wall to protect it from ulcers
options.C: It stimulates the release of bile from the liver
options.D: It neutralizes excess stomach acid

explanation: Chief cells release pepsinogen as a safe, inactive form. Once stomach acid hits it, it turns into active pepsin to start chopping up proteins! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h4)

question: How does gender inequality directly contribute to early marriage?

options.A: By forcing boys to leave school early to work
options.B: By limiting educational opportunities for young girls
options.C: By granting young females absolute control over family assets
options.D: By making traditional marriage ceremonies illegal

explanation: When girls are denied education and future opportunities, society often pushes them straight into early marriage instead.

question: Which of these structures is part of the upper respiratory tract?

options.A: The pleural cavity
options.B: The pharynx
options.C: The alveoli
options.D: The bronchioles

explanation: You got it! The upper tract includes the nose, sinuses, and pharynx, while tiny air sacs like alveoli are deep down in the lower tract.

question: What is one of the main goals of maternal health services in a displacement camp?

options.A: Providing free formula milk to every newborn infant
options.B: Reducing maternal and neonatal mortality through skilled care
options.C: Eliminating the need for any antenatal checkups
options.D: Mandating home deliveries without professional assistance

explanation: Every mother deserves a safe delivery! Providing skilled midwives and emergency obstetric care saves mothers and newborns from avoidable complications in crisis zones.

question: Which of the following is a primary goal of conducting epidemiological studies?

options.A: Replacing bedside clinical nurses with data entry clerks
options.B: Eliminating the need for patient consent in research trials
options.C: Providing a foundation for public health policy and disease control
options.D: Ensuring that all hospitals maintain identical financial budgets

explanation: Epidemiology isn't just about numbers—it gives health leaders the real-world evidence they need to build strong health policies and stop outbreaks.

question: What is the main goal of planning emergency transport and money before labor starts?

options.A: To replace the need for professional skilled attendants at birth
options.B: To guarantee that the mother will have a completely painless delivery
options.C: To eliminate costly delays when unexpected complications strike
options.D: To ensure the baby is born precisely on the expected due date

explanation: Exactly right! Having transport and funds ready ahead of time saves precious minutes and prevents dangerous delays if an emergency happens.

question: Why does an injured area of the body become swollen, red, and warm?

options.A: Antibodies are tickling local nerve endings
options.B: Extra blood and fluid leak from widened blood vessels into the tissue
options.C: Cold blood gets trapped inside the injury
options.D: Bacteria are multiplying and generating heat

explanation: More blood rushes to the injury to help heal it, and fluid leaks out into the tissues, causing that familiar swelling and warmth.

question: In the Health Belief Model, what do we mean by 'perceived susceptibility'?

options.A: A reminder from a family member to visit the clinic
options.B: Believing one is at risk for a health problem
options.C: The financial cost of buying hospital drugs
options.D: Thinking a disease has no cure at all

explanation: Perceived susceptibility is simply a person's mindset of 'Could this sickness happen to me?' It's about personal vulnerability.

question: Why should the vertical axis on a bar chart usually start at zero?

options.A: To make all the bars look exactly the same height
options.B: To hide negative values from the reader
options.C: To prevent exaggerating small differences between groups
options.D: To ensure the chart fits onto a standard notebook page

explanation: Starting at zero maintains correct visual proportions so readers do not misinterpret minor changes as massive clinical differences. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary function of cerebrospinal fluid?

options.A: To transmit electrical signals across synapses
options.B: To cushion the brain and provide nutritional support
options.C: To produce red blood cells for nervous tissue
options.D: To cool down the body during a high fever

explanation: CSF acts as a shock-absorbing liquid cushion while also nourishing the central nervous system tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h7)

question: How do vitamins and minerals often help enzymes do their work?

options.A: They turn into glucose to provide extra energy for the brain.
options.B: They act as coenzymes and cofactors to help enzymes function.
options.C: They slow down metabolism to prevent the body from overheating.
options.D: They replace enzymes when the body runs out of protein.

explanation: Many vitamins and minerals team up with enzymes as coenzymes or cofactors, acting like a key that unlocks the enzyme's full working potential!

question: A baby is born limp, pale, and quiet after a home delivery. What should you do right away?

options.A: Immediately give the baby back to the mother for skin-to-skin contact
options.B: Wait patiently for five minutes to see if the Apgar score improves
options.C: Call an ambulance without taking any action inside the home
options.D: Provide initial steps of warmth, clearing the airway, and stimulation

explanation: Act fast and stay calm! A baby who isn't breathing needs immediate help: dry them, keep them warm, clear the airway, and gently stimulate them.

question: A patient calls the clinic worried because she has heavy cramps and is passing large clots after taking misoprostol. As a nurse, how do you view this?

options.A: It means the entire treatment has completely failed.
options.B: It is the expected normal physical response to the drugs.
options.C: It indicates a dangerous uterine rupture.
options.D: It is a sign of a severe medication allergy.

explanation: Brilliant! Heavy cramping and passing clots show that the medication is working and the uterus is emptying as it should.

question: What is a major benefit of using video conferencing for patient follow-up care?

options.A: It bridges geographical gaps for patients in remote areas
options.B: It completely replaces the need for any in-person hospital visits
options.C: It removes all requirements for patient data privacy protection
options.D: It allows nurses to physically change dressings from miles away

explanation: Video tools allow nurses to assess and support patients who live far away without requiring them to travel to the facility. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h3)

question: A midwife wants to gain the trust of a conservative community before introducing family planning education. What is the best initial step?

options.A: Distribute pamphlets written in a complex medical language
options.B: Listen actively to local concerns and respect cultural sensitivities
options.C: Demand that the village chief close down all local shrines
options.D: Threaten residents with withdrawal of all general healthcare

explanation: Building trust requires listening and showing respect for local culture before attempting to introduce sensitive health topics. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h6)

question: What approach should a nurse use when caring for a patient experiencing complications from a harmful traditional practice?

options.A: Trauma-informed and non-judgmental care
options.B: Strict detachment with no emotional conversation
options.C: Refusal of treatment until legal charges are filed
options.D: Immediate public shaming to deter future acts

explanation: Patients must feel safe and respected to build trust and accept necessary medical and psychological support. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h6)

question: What is a key nursing duty right after a patient finishes an MRI where they received mild sedation?

options.A: Restrict fluid intake for the next twelve hours to prevent swelling
options.B: Encourage the patient to walk briskly around the unit to clear the drugs
options.C: Monitor vital signs and level of consciousness until the sedative wears off
options.D: Perform a complete neurological exam every five minutes for two hours

explanation: You got it! Keeping a close eye on vital signs and alertness helps ensure the patient safely recovers from the sedative.

question: Which of these is a dangerous method often seen in back-alley or clandestine terminations?

options.A: Receiving intravenous fluids at a primary health centre
options.B: Taking oral contraceptive pills prescribed by a pharmacist
options.C: Undergoing ultrasound scanning in a private clinic
options.D: Inserting sharp sticks or knitting needles into the uterus

explanation: Well done. Using crude objects like sticks is extremely dangerous and can easily cause severe bleeding and organ damage.

question: What are the three parts of the epidemiological triad used to study how diseases spread?

options.A: Infection, disease, and recovery
options.B: Pathogen, vector, and symptom
options.C: Agent, host, and environment
options.D: Human, animal, and bacteria

explanation: Think of the triad as a stool with three legs: the infectious agent, the susceptible host, and the environment. All three must interact for an infection to take root!

question: What is the main reason nurses use quick screening tools like the CAGE questionnaire?

options.A: To measure the exact level of vitamins present in the bloodstream
options.B: To quickly identify potential substance abuse or dependence problems
options.C: To calculate the correct dosage of emergency antidote medication
options.D: To diagnose specific mental health disorders like major depression

explanation: Exactly! Screening tools are short, easy-to-use questions that help us spot patients who might need a closer look or professional support for substance use.

question: Which of the following is a classic danger sign in pregnancy that a patient must report immediately?

options.A: Vaginal bleeding
options.B: Normal fetal movement
options.C: Mild morning sickness
options.D: Occasional mild backache

explanation: You got it! Vaginal bleeding at any point in pregnancy is never normal—it can point to serious issues like placenta previa and needs quick medical attention.

question: A patient with severe schizophrenia is losing weight because they never cook or buy groceries. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: A physical inability to chew or swallow solid food
options.B: An allergic reaction to standard grocery store items
options.C: Negative symptoms like apathy and lack of drive
options.D: A deliberate choice to fast for religious reasons

explanation: Well done! Negative symptoms such as avolition can rob patients of the motivation needed to plan and execute daily tasks like cooking.

question: Why would a doctor order a 24-hour Holter monitor for a patient with occasional dizzy spells?

options.A: To continuously measure the oxygen saturation levels in the blood overnight
options.B: To deliver mild electrical shocks if the patient's heart rate drops too low
options.C: To catch intermittent dysrhythmias that do not happen during a quick clinic visit
options.D: To permanently replace the need for an invasive cardiac catheterization

explanation: Some heart flutters only happen once in a while. A 24-hour Holter monitor records the rhythm all day and night at home, helping catch those sneaky, unpredictable episodes!

question: What do we call the practice of breaking a big ward workload into smaller tasks and giving them out based on staff skills?

options.A: Span of control
options.B: Division of labour
options.C: Centralisation
options.D: Delegation

explanation: You got it! Division of labour splits a heavy job into manageable pieces so everyone can focus on what they do best.

question: What is the main responsibility of the nurse at the bedside during unit dispensing?

options.A: Checking the chemical purity of drugs inside the pharmacy lab
options.B: Packaging the individual pills into small plastic wrappers
options.C: Performing final safety checks and administering the drug
options.D: Calculating the bulk wholesale cost of each medication dose

explanation: The nurse is the last person to see the patient before ingestion, making bedside verification essential to catch any lingering errors. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is a rectovaginal fistula often psychologically distressing for a patient?

options.A: It causes continuous involuntary passage of gas and stool vaginally
options.B: It prevents the patient from ever walking again
options.C: It causes severe upper abdominal pain after meals
options.D: It immediately leads to total kidney failure

explanation: The uncontrollable leakage of feces and flatus through the vagina causes significant hygiene challenges and social embarrassment. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h1)

question: What cultural belief often causes many communities to tolerate domestic violence?

options.A: Immediate community intervention during family disputes
options.B: Universal access to legal education for all citizens
options.C: Equal economic power sharing between men and women
options.D: Normalization of patriarchal dominance and domestic discipline

explanation: You're doing great! In many places, old-school cultural norms wrongly frame male control and physical correction as normal or acceptable.

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for a dying patient?

options.A: Forcing the patient through all five stages of grief
options.B: Maximizing comfort, dignity, and holistic support
options.C: Finding a miracle cure for the disease
options.D: Restricting visitors to keep the room quiet

explanation: At the end of life, our main duty as nurses is palliative care: keeping them comfortable, pain-free, and deeply respected.

question: Which blood test is used to monitor the therapeutic level of the anticoagulant warfarin?

options.A: White blood cell differential
options.B: Fast blood glucose level
options.C: International Normalized Ratio
options.D: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate

explanation: The International Normalized Ratio measures how long it takes for a patient's blood to clot while taking warfarin. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility regarding vaccine storage at a health facility?

options.A: Repairing broken compressors in refrigerator units
options.B: Checking and logging refrigerator temperatures twice daily
options.C: Testing the chemical composition of each vaccine vial
options.D: Ordering new vaccine stocks directly from foreign factories

explanation: Nurses must monitor and record storage temperatures regularly to catch equipment failures before vaccines are ruined. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h4)

question: A healthy family member who was exposed to measles is asked to stay at home and avoid contact with others for a short period. What is this control measure called?

options.A: Quarantine
options.B: Isolation
options.C: Active immunization
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: You got it! Quarantine is used for healthy people who were exposed, to watch if they develop symptoms, whereas isolation is for people who are already sick.

question: What is a major job of minerals like calcium in the human body?

options.A: Insulating internal organs against cold temperatures
options.B: Building strong bones and transmitting nerve signals
options.C: Providing the bulk needed for regular bowel movements
options.D: Serving as the primary energy source for running

explanation: Minerals do heavy lifting behind the scenes. Calcium builds strong bones and teeth, and helps your nerves and muscles communicate smoothly!

question: Why is teaching community members about injection safety so important in Nigeria?

options.A: To cut down the cost of running clinics
options.B: To replace nursing school training
options.C: To help patients understand they don't always need an injection
options.D: To teach patients to give themselves IV drugs at home

explanation: Many people believe injections work faster than tablets, leading to a huge demand for unnecessary shots. Educating the public keeps everyone safer.

question: Why should you give extra time when doing a mental assessment on an older adult?

options.A: Rushing can cause anxiety and lead to inaccurate assessment results
options.B: Older adults legally require thirty minutes per interview question
options.C: It gives the nurse time to complete paperwork during the session
options.D: Slowing down prevents the patient from hearing the questions

explanation: Thinking takes a little longer with age, so patience helps you get accurate answers and keeps the patient calm.

question: Why are single-dose medication vials much better for infection control than multi-dose vials?

options.A: They completely eliminate the risk of cross-contamination between patients
options.B: They contain larger volumes of liquid for multiple shifts
options.C: They are always cheaper for hospital procurement to buy
options.D: They never require alcohol swabbing of the rubber top

explanation: You got it! Since single-dose vials are used for just one patient, there's zero chance of a contaminated needle transferring germs to the next dose. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h7)

question: A ward tries a new handwashing protocol. After one month, how do they check if it's working?

options.A: Assume it's working because nobody complained at the meeting
options.B: Compare current audit data against the baseline measurements taken before starting
options.C: Wait five years before checking infection stats
options.D: Ask the head nurse if the ward looks cleaner

explanation: Brilliant! You always compare your current results to your original baseline. Numbers don't lie, and it's the only way to prove real progress.

question: Why does batch cooking help save money?

options.A: It guarantees that food will never spoil under any condition
options.B: It requires buying expensive kitchen appliances upfront
options.C: It forces family members to eat less food overall
options.D: It reduces energy consumption and limits ingredient waste

explanation: Spot on! Cooking larger pots at once uses less cooking gas or kerosene and ensures ingredients get used up before going bad.

question: What is a major challenge in providing adolescent reproductive care in many communities?

options.A: The requirement that all nurses undergo legal training before practice
options.B: A complete lack of teenage patients visiting urban health facilities
options.C: Conflict between traditional moral disapproval and young people's health needs
options.D: An absolute nationwide ban on importing any modern contraceptive items

explanation: Cultural and religious beliefs often clash with the clinical reality that teens need reproductive health support. Navigating this is part of nursing!

question: What is a major feature of our innate immune system?

options.A: Slow and highly targeted
options.B: Dependent on prior exposure
options.C: Exclusive to viral infections
options.D: Rapid and non-specific

explanation: Innate immunity acts immediately! It doesn't need to 'remember' a past infection; it fights back right away using the same general tactics every time.

question: How do communication breakdowns between hospital departments affect the DRF exemption process?

options.A: They force the federal government to send more medical equipment
options.B: They cause delays in patient care and lead to lost exemption vouchers
options.C: They automatically increase the overall monthly revenue of the pharmacy
options.D: They improve the working relationship between doctors and pharmacists

explanation: When departments fail to communicate well, vulnerable patients suffer dangerous delays while waiting for their paperwork to clear.

question: What is the primary purpose of the review of systems in health history taking?

options.A: To perform the physical hands-on examination of the body
options.B: To discharge the patient from the hospital ward
options.C: To uncover symptoms the patient may have forgotten or overlooked
options.D: To administer prescribed medications to the patient

explanation: The review of systems uses a systematic checklist to catch extra details the patient did not bring up initially. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h6)

question: What makes an 'android' pelvis shape stand out?

options.A: It is heart-shaped with prominent ischial spines
options.B: It is narrow and oval with a very long front-to-back measurement
options.C: It is flat and wide with a short front-to-back diameter
options.D: It is a classic round shape found in most females

explanation: An android pelvis is more like a male pelvis, featuring a heart-shaped opening that can sometimes make labor a bit tricky.

question: How are the tiny bony struts inside cancellous bone arranged?

options.A: In a random web with no fixed pattern
options.B: In circular rings around a central canal
options.C: Along lines of physical stress
options.D: In thick parallel sheets along the bone shaft

explanation: Think of how a bridge is built to handle heavy loads! These tiny struts (called trabeculae) arrange themselves dynamically right along the lines where the bone feels the most physical stress and pressure from daily movement.

question: How long does morning stiffness typically last for someone with osteoarthritis?

options.A: Only occurring late at night
options.B: Less than thirty minutes
options.C: Several hours throughout the day
options.D: All day without any relief

explanation: Correct! OA morning stiffness is usually brief—lasting under thirty minutes—which helps doctors tell it apart from other inflammatory joint problems.

question: A new mother at a health post starts bleeding heavily and looks dizzy and pale. What are your first nursing steps?

options.A: Encourage the patient to stand up and walk around to stimulate circulation
options.B: Apply a warm compress to the patient's forehead and offer oral fluids
options.C: Wait quietly for two hours to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.D: Perform uterine massage, give oxytocin, and prepare for emergency referral

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage is an emergency. Massaging the uterus and giving oxytocin helps it contract while you arrange urgent transfer.

question: Why is a single initial assessment insufficient for palliative care patients?

options.A: Palliative conditions and symptoms change rapidly over time
options.B: Patients usually forget their medical history on day one
options.C: Doctors prefer to change diagnoses daily without reason
options.D: Hospitals require a new paperwork form every single hour

explanation: Because disease trajectories fluctuate, ongoing re-assessment is necessary to catch new or worsening symptoms. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h2)

question: What do we call 'diagnostic overshadowing' when caring for a patient with a disability?

options.A: Overprescribing pain relief medication for chronic joint stiffness
options.B: Failing to document medical history correctly in the patient chart
options.C: Using outdated diagnostic machinery during routine check-ups
options.D: Attributing all new symptoms mistakenly to the existing disability

explanation: It's a sneaky trap! This happens when we assume a new problem is just 'part of their usual condition' and forget to investigate properly. Always look closer!

question: Which plant is the natural source for the heart medication digoxin?

options.A: Cinchona tree
options.B: Foxglove plant
options.C: Opium poppy
options.D: Deadly nightshade

explanation: Digoxin comes straight from the lovely foxglove plant to help strengthen and regulate heart contractions. Plants are amazing pharmacies!

question: Which layer of the meninges is the tough, outermost layer attached to the skull?

options.A: Choroid plexus
options.B: Arachnoid mater
options.C: Dura mater
options.D: Pia mater

explanation: The dura mater is a thick, durable membrane providing sturdy outer protection for the brain and spinal cord. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which set of symptoms points strongly to acute chest syndrome in a hospital patient?

options.A: Painful swelling of the hands and feet
options.B: Yellow skin, dark urine, and severe fatigue
options.C: Chest pain, fever, and a new cough
options.D: Headache, dizziness, and sudden blurry vision

explanation: Spotting acute chest syndrome early is a key nursing skill. It acts a lot like pneumonia, showing up with chest pain, fever, and coughing because sickled cells or infections get trapped in the lungs.

question: Why won't hormonal emergency pills work if a woman has already ovulated?

options.A: Because the hormone dose is too low to stay in the stomach
options.B: Because the egg has already been released and is available for fertilization
options.C: Because ovulation automatically neutralizes all chemical drugs
options.D: Because the uterine lining instantly sheds upon ovulation

explanation: Remember, these pills work by delaying ovulation. If the egg has already been released, the pill is too late to stop it from meeting a sperm. Makes total sense, right?

question: Which of these is NOT a typical source of unwanted clinical variation?

options.A: Differences in individual clinician training and experience
options.B: Following strict, up-to-date evidence-based protocols
options.C: Inconsistent communication during nursing shift handovers
options.D: Varying availability of necessary medical supplies on wards

explanation: Exactly! Following solid, research-backed protocols actually reduces unwanted differences and helps us give better care.
